cbc91582-8d44-5de1-9c98-1c5de173eefb.title: Applying De Moivre's Theorem With a Negative Sine

e-5271.worked_solution:
De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
\left[ \cos(\varphi) + \textrm{i}\sin(\varphi) \right]^n = \cos(n\varphi) + \textrm{i}\sin{(n\varphi)}.
$$

In our expression, we have $n=4$ and $\varphi=\dfrac{\theta}{10}.$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\theta }{10})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\theta }{10})]}^{4} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\theta }{10})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\theta }{10}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\theta }{5})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\theta }{5}).\end{aligned}
$$

e-5270.knowledge_point: Applying De Moivre's Theorem to Fractions
e-5270.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\dfrac{1}{\left[ \cos(\theta) +\textrm{i}\sin(\theta) \right]^2} = \left[ \cos(\theta) +\textrm{i}\sin(\theta) \right]^{-2} .
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
\left[ \cos(\varphi) + \textrm{i}\sin(\varphi) \right]^n = \cos(n\varphi) + \textrm{i}\sin{(n\varphi)}.
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-2$ and $\varphi=\theta.$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{2}} & ={[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{-2} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-2\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-2\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\cos(-\varphi) = \cos (\varphi)$ and $\sin(-\varphi) = -\sin(\varphi)$ for any input $\varphi,$ we have

$$
\cos(-2\theta) + \textrm{i}\sin(-2\theta) = \cos(2\theta) - \textrm{i}\sin{(2\theta)}.
$$

e-5291.knowledge_point: Applying De Moivre's Theorem With a Negative Sine
e-5291.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )]}^{4}} & ={[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )]}^{-4}.\end{aligned}
$$

For expressions involving subtraction, De Moivre's theorem states that

$$
\left[ \cos (\varphi) - \textrm{i}\sin(\varphi) \right]^n = \cos(n\varphi) - \textrm{i}\sin{(n\varphi)}.
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-4$ and $\varphi=2\theta.$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )]}^{-4} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-4\cdot 2\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-4\cdot 2\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-8\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-8\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\cos(-\varphi) = \cos (\varphi)$ and $\sin(-\varphi) = -\sin(\varphi)$ for any input $\varphi,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-8\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-8\theta ) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )-[-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta )] \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Simplify the expression [cos⁡(2θ5)+isin⁡(2θ5)]20.

a
20[cos⁡(2θ5)+isin⁡(2θ5)]
b
cos⁡(8θ)+isin⁡(8θ)
c
25(cos⁡(20θ)+isin⁡(20θ))
d
cos⁡(20θ)+isin⁡(20θ)
e
cos⁡(4θ)+isin⁡(4θ)
Submit

decision.explanation: By De Moivre's theorem, multiply the angle by 20: 20(2θ/5)=8θ. The result is cos(8θ)+i sin(8θ), matching option b.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=20$ and $\phi =\frac{2\theta }{5}.$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\theta }{5})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\theta }{5})]}^{20} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(20\cdot \frac{2\theta }{5})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(20\cdot \frac{2\theta }{5}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Simplify the expression [cos⁡(2θ5)+isin⁡(2θ5)]20.

a
20[cos⁡(2θ5)+isin⁡(2θ5)]
b
cos⁡(8θ)+isin⁡(8θ)
c
25(cos⁡(20θ)+isin⁡(20θ))
d
cos⁡(20θ)+isin⁡(20θ)
e
cos⁡(4θ)+isin⁡(4θ)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

De Moivre's Theorem states that [cos⁡(φ)+isin⁡(φ)]n=cos⁡(nφ)+isin⁡(nφ).

In our expression, we have n=20 and φ=2θ5. Substituting in these values, we get

[cos⁡(2θ5)+isin⁡(2θ5)]20=cos⁡(20⋅2θ5)+isin⁡(20⋅2θ5)=cos⁡(8θ)+isin⁡(8θ).

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that De Moivre's theorem multiplies the angle by 20: 20(2θ/5)=8θ. Therefore option b is correct; multiplying the entire expression by 20, as in the deliberately incorrect submission, is invalid.

content.worked_solution:
De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=20$ and $\phi =\frac{2\theta }{5}.$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\theta }{5})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\theta }{5})]}^{20} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(20\cdot \frac{2\theta }{5})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(20\cdot \frac{2\theta }{5}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6

Simplify the expression 2[cos⁡θ+isin⁡θ]12.

a
2[cos⁡(6θ)−isin⁡(6θ)]
b
2[cos⁡(12θ)−isin⁡(12θ)]
c
2[cos⁡(θ12)−isin⁡(θ12)]

e
6[cos⁡θ−isin⁡θ]
Submit

decision.explanation: Rewrite the expression as 2[cos(θ)+i sin(θ)]^(-12). De Moivre's theorem gives 2[cos(-12θ)+i sin(-12θ)]=2[cos(12θ)-i sin(12θ)], matching option b.

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]}^{12}}={[\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]}^{-12}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]}^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-12$ and $\phi =\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]}^{12}} & =2{[\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]}^{-12} \\  & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-12\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-12\theta )].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-12\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-12\theta )]=2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(12\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(12\theta )].
$$

Question 6
?

Simplify the expression 2[cos⁡θ+isin⁡θ]12.

a
2[cos⁡(6θ)−isin⁡(6θ)]
b
2[cos⁡(12θ)−isin⁡(12θ)]
c
2[cos⁡(θ12)−isin⁡(θ12)]
d
cos⁡(θ6)−isin⁡(θ6)
e
6[cos⁡θ−isin⁡θ]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, note that 1[cos⁡θ+isin⁡θ]12=[cos⁡θ+isin⁡θ]−12.

De Moivre's Theorem states that [cos⁡(φ)+isin⁡(φ)]n=cos⁡(nφ)+isin⁡(nφ).

In our expression, we have n=−12 and φ=θ. Substituting in these values, we get 2[cos⁡θ+isin⁡θ]12=2[cos⁡θ+isin⁡θ]−12=2[cos⁡(−12θ)+isin⁡(−12θ)].

Finally, using the fact that cos⁡(−φ)=cos⁡(φ) and sin⁡(−φ)=−sin⁡(φ) for any input φ, we have 2[cos⁡(−12θ)+isin⁡(−12θ)]=2[cos⁡(12θ)−isin⁡(12θ)].

content.knowledge_point: Applying De Moivre's Theorem to Fractions
content.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]}^{12}}={[\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]}^{-12}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]}^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-12$ and $\phi =\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]}^{12}} & =2{[\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]}^{-12} \\  & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-12\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-12\theta )].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-12\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-12\theta )]=2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(12\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(12\theta )].
$$

Question 7
?

Simplify the expression 6[cos⁡3θ+isin⁡3θ]5.

a
30[cos⁡(3θ)−isin⁡(3θ)]
b
6[cos⁡(15θ)−isin⁡(15θ)]
c
65[cos⁡(3θ)−isin⁡(3θ)]
d
2[cos⁡(θ5)−isin⁡(θ5)]
e
6[cos⁡(3θ5)−isin⁡(3θ5)]
Submit

decision.explanation: Rewrite the expression as 6[cos(3θ)+i sin(3θ)]^(-5). De Moivre's theorem gives 6[cos(-15θ)+i sin(-15θ)]=6[cos(15θ)-i sin(15θ)], matching option b.

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\frac{1}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡3\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta ]^{5}}=[\operatorname{cos}⁡3\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta ]^{-5}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
[\operatorname{cos}⁡\phi +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\phi ]^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-5$ and $\phi =3\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡3\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta ]^{5}} & =6[\operatorname{cos}⁡3\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta ]^{-5} \\  & =6[\operatorname{cos}⁡(3(-5)\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3(-5)\theta )] \\  & =6[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-15\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-15\theta )].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
6[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-15\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-15\theta )]=6[\operatorname{cos}⁡(15\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(15\theta )].
$$

Question 7

Simplify the expression 6[cos⁡3θ+isin⁡3θ]5.

a
30[cos⁡(3θ)−isin⁡(3θ)]
b
6[cos⁡(15θ)−isin⁡(15θ)]
c
65[cos⁡(3θ)−isin⁡(3θ)]
d
2[cos⁡(θ5)−isin⁡(θ5)]
e
6[cos⁡(3θ5)−isin⁡(3θ5)]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, note that 1[cos⁡3θ+isin⁡3θ]5=[cos⁡3θ+isin⁡3θ]−5.

De Moivre's Theorem states that [cos⁡φ+isin⁡φ]n=cos⁡(nφ)+isin⁡(nφ).

In our expression, we have n=−5 and φ=3θ. Substituting in these values, we get 6[cos⁡3θ+isin⁡3θ]5=6[cos⁡3θ+isin⁡3θ]−5=6[cos⁡(3(−5)θ)+isin⁡(3(−5)θ)]=6[cos⁡(−15θ)+isin⁡(−15θ)].

Finally, using the fact that cos⁡(−φ)=cos⁡(φ) and sin⁡(−φ)=−sin⁡(φ) for any input φ, we have 6[cos⁡(−15θ)+isin⁡(−15θ)]=6[cos⁡(15θ)−isin⁡(15θ)].

content.knowledge_point: Applying De Moivre's Theorem to Fractions
content.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\frac{1}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡3\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta ]^{5}}=[\operatorname{cos}⁡3\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta ]^{-5}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
[\operatorname{cos}⁡\phi +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\phi ]^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-5$ and $\phi =3\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡3\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta ]^{5}} & =6[\operatorname{cos}⁡3\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta ]^{-5} \\  & =6[\operatorname{cos}⁡(3(-5)\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3(-5)\theta )] \\  & =6[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-15\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-15\theta )].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
6[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-15\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-15\theta )]=6[\operatorname{cos}⁡(15\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(15\theta )].
$$

Simplify the expression 1[cos⁡(5θ)+isin⁡(5θ)]6.

a
2cos⁡(15θ)+2isin⁡(15θ)
b
cos⁡(30θ)+isin⁡(30θ)
c
cos⁡(30θ)−isin⁡(30θ)
d
5cos⁡(6θ)−5isin⁡(6θ)
e
cos⁡(15θ)−isin⁡(15θ)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, note that 1[cos⁡(5θ)+isin⁡(5θ)]6=[cos⁡(5θ)+isin⁡(5θ)]−6.

De Moivre's Theorem states that [cos⁡(φ)+isin⁡(φ)]n=cos⁡(nφ)+isin⁡(nφ).

In our expression, we have n=−6 and φ=5θ. Substituting in these values, we get 1[cos⁡(5θ)+isin⁡(5θ)]6=[cos⁡(5θ)+isin⁡(5θ)]−6=cos⁡(−30θ)+isin⁡(−30θ).

Finally, using the fact that cos⁡(−φ)=cos⁡(φ) and sin⁡(−φ)=−sin⁡(φ) for any input φ, we have cos⁡(−30θ)+isin⁡(−30θ)=cos⁡(30θ)−isin⁡(30θ).

Question 9
?

Simplify the expression 1[cos⁡(θ)+isin⁡(θ)]6.

a
6cos⁡(θ)+6isin⁡(θ)
b
cos⁡(6θ)+isin⁡(6θ)
c
cos⁡(6θ)−isin⁡(6θ)
d
2cos⁡(3θ)+2isin⁡(3θ)
e
3cos⁡(2θ)−3isin⁡(2θ)
Submit

decision.explanation: The reciprocal gives exponent −6. By De Moivre's theorem, the expression equals cos(−6θ)+i sin(−6θ)=cos(6θ)−i sin(6θ), matching option c.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{6}}={[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{-6}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]}^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-6$ and $\phi =\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{6}} & ={[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{-6} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-6\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-6\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(-6\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-6\theta )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\theta ).
$$

Question 9
?

Simplify the expression 1[cos⁡(θ)+isin⁡(θ)]6.

a
6cos⁡(θ)+6isin⁡(θ)
b
cos⁡(6θ)+isin⁡(6θ)
c
cos⁡(6θ)−isin⁡(6θ)
d
2cos⁡(3θ)+2isin⁡(3θ)
e
3cos⁡(2θ)−3isin⁡(2θ)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, note that 1[cos⁡(θ)+isin⁡(θ)]6=[cos⁡(θ)+isin⁡(θ)]−6.

De Moivre's Theorem states that [cos⁡(φ)+isin⁡(φ)]n=cos⁡(nφ)+isin⁡(nφ).

In our expression, we have n=−6 and φ=θ. Substituting in these values, we get 1[cos⁡(θ)+isin⁡(θ)]6=[cos⁡(θ)+isin⁡(θ)]−6=cos⁡(−6θ)+isin⁡(−6θ).

Finally, using the fact that cos⁡(−φ)=cos⁡(φ) and sin⁡(−φ)=−sin⁡(φ) for any input φ, we have cos⁡(−6θ)+isin⁡(−6θ)=cos⁡(6θ)−isin⁡(6θ).

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option c. The reciprocal gives exponent −6, so De Moivre's theorem yields cos(−6θ)+i sin(−6θ)=cos(6θ)−i sin(6θ).

content.knowledge_point: Applying De Moivre's Theorem to Fractions
content.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{6}}={[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{-6}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]}^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-6$ and $\phi =\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{6}} & ={[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{-6} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-6\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-6\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(-6\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-6\theta )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\theta ).
$$

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\frac{2}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]^{4}}=2[\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]^{-4}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
[\operatorname{cos}⁡\phi +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\phi ]^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-4$ and $\phi =2\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]^{4}} & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]^{-4} \\  & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2(-4)\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2(-4)\theta )] \\  & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-8\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-8\theta )].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-8\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-8\theta )]=2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta )].
$$

Correct
EXPLANATION

First, note that 2[cos⁡2θ+isin⁡2θ]4=2[cos⁡2θ+isin⁡2θ]−4.

De Moivre's Theorem states that [cos⁡φ+isin⁡φ]n=cos⁡(nφ)+isin⁡(nφ).

In our expression, we have n=−4 and φ=2θ. Substituting in these values, we get 2[cos⁡2θ+isin⁡2θ]4=2[cos⁡2θ+isin⁡2θ]−4=2[cos⁡(2(−4)θ)+isin⁡(2(−4)θ)]=2[cos⁡(−8θ)+isin⁡(−8θ)].

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]^{4}} & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]^{-4} \\  & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2(-4)\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2(-4)\theta )] \\  & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-8\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-8\theta )].\end{aligned}

{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]}^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).

For expressions involving subtraction, De Moivre's theorem states that [cos⁡(φ)−isin⁡(φ)]n=cos⁡(nφ)−isin⁡(nφ).

after.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{6}} & ={[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{-6}.\end{aligned}
$$

For expressions involving subtraction, De Moivre's theorem states that

$$
{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]}^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-6$ and $\phi =\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{-6}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(-6\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-6\theta )
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-6\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-6\theta ) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\theta )-[-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\theta )] \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

cos⁡(−6θ)−isin⁡(−6θ)=cos⁡(6θ)−[−isin⁡(6θ)]=cos⁡(6θ)+isin⁡(6θ).
